question.problem:
Find the point(s) of the intersection of the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=9$ and the line 
$\{\begin{aligned}x=t \\ y=t-3, \\ z=t\end{aligned}$ where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
question.worked_solution:
Substituting the expressions for $x$, $y$, and $z$ from the parametric equation of the line into the equation of the sphere, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =9 \\ (t)^{2}+(t-3)^{2}+(t)^{2} & =9 \\ {t}^{2}+({t}^{2}-6t+9)+{t}^{2} & =9 \\ 3{t}^{2}-6t+9 & =9 \\ 3{t}^{2}-6t & =0 \\ t(t-2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we get the solutions $t=0$ and $t=2.$ 

Now, we substitute our solutions back into the equations of the line.

- For $t=0$, we have

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=(0)=0 \\ y=(0)-3=-3 \\ z=(0)=0,\end{aligned}
$$

so the first point is $(0,-3,0).$

- For $t=2$, we have

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=(2)=2 \\ y=(2)-3=-1 \\ z=(2)=2,\end{aligned}
$$

so the second point is $(2,-1,2).$

Therefore, the points of intersection are $(0,-3,0)$ and $(2,-1,2).$
